name: Lip Reading Accuracy Score
description: Computes lip reading accuracy by comparing visual speech with audio — deepfakes often have mismatched lip movements.
algorithm: Lip Reading Accuracy Score Analysis Algorithm
mechanism:
This method performs lip reading analysis for audio-visual deepfake detection:

1. **Visual Speech Feature Extraction**: Lip region is cropped and normalized per frame, extracting visual speech features — lip shape (inner/outer contour), lip area, mouth opening, tongue visibility, and teeth exposure. These features encode the visual aspect of speech articulation (visemes).

2. **Viseme Sequence Decoding**: The visual speech features are analyzed to determine which phonological units (visemes) are being articulated. Visemes are decoded from the lip motion sequence using temporal pattern recognition.

3. **Audio-Visual Concordance**: Decoded visual phonemes are compared with phonemes derived from the audio speech signal. In authentic video, visual and audio phonemes should match — the lips should form shapes corresponding to the spoken sounds. Deepfakes with mismatched audio may show visual-audio phoneme disagreements per Chung & Zisserman (2017).

4. **Articulation Quality Assessment**: Natural speech articulation involves precisely coordinated lip, tongue, jaw, and cheek movements. The method evaluates articulation quality — whether lip shapes fully achieve the target viseme positions. Deepfake lip generation may produce under-articulated or over-simplified lip movements that approximate but don't fully achieve correct viseme shapes.

5. **Coarticulation Analysis**: In natural speech, phoneme production is influenced by surrounding phonemes (coarticulation) — the lips begin transitioning to the next sound before completing the current one. The method checks for natural coarticulation effects. AI lip generation may produce discrete viseme transitions without the smooth blending of coarticulation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
